Should countries restrict open-source AI? Argue 4 positions: completely open, partially restricted, heavily restricted, and outright banned. For each, give the strongest steelman, the typical counter-argument, and one historical analogy.

message.content:
# Four Positions on Open-Source AI Restriction

---

## 1. Completely Open

**Steelman:**
The open-source movement has been one of humanity's greatest engines of innovation and safety. Transparency enables global scrutiny—thousands of researchers can identify vulnerabilities, audit biases, and improve safety faster than any closed lab could alone. Restricting AI creates dangerous power concentrates in a handful of corporations or states, which historically pose far greater risks than distributed, democratized technology. The argument that AI is "too dangerous to release" echoes every previous technological moral panic—from the printing press to the internet to cryptography—and society ultimately benefited from openness in each case. Closed systems fail quietly and catastrophically; open systems fail loudly and visibly, allowing correction.

**Typical Counter-argument:**
AI is categorically different from previous open-source technologies. A language model cannot be "recalled" once released; it can be copied
